question.problem:
Consider the following data sets:

$$
x=\{5,\,8,\,2\},\,y=\{-1,\,2,\,5\}
$$

You are given that $\overset{―}{x}=5$ and $\overset{―}{y}=2.$ Calculate the corresponding linear correlation coefficient.
question.worked_solution:
The linear correlation coefficient $\rho $ of the data sets $x=\{{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}\}$ and $y=\{{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}\}$ is given by 

$$
\rho (x,y)=\frac{\text{Cov}(x,y)}{{\sigma }_{x}\cdot {\sigma }_{y}}=\frac{{S}_{xy}}{\sqrt{{S}_{xx}\cdot {S}_{yy}}}.
$$

First, we compute the sum in the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =(5-5)(-1-2)+(8-5)(2-2)+(2-5)(5-2) \\  & =(0)(-3)+(3)(0)+(-3)(3) \\  & =0+0-9 \\  & =-9\end{aligned}
$$

Second, we compute the sums in the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{xx} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =(5-5)^{2}+(8-5)^{2}+(2-5)^{2} \\  & =0+9+9 \\  & =18 \\ {S}_{yy} & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y})^{2} \\  & =(-1-2)^{2}+(2-2)^{2}+(5-2)^{2} \\  & =9+0+9 \\  & =18\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we use the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho (x,y) & =\frac{(-9)}{\sqrt{18}\cdot \sqrt{18}} \\  & =-\frac{-9}{3\sqrt{2}\cdot 3\sqrt{2}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2} \\  & =-0.5\end{aligned}
$$
